name: Niandra Lades And Usually Just A T-Shirt

info.desc: Niandra Lades and Usually Just a T-Shirt is the debut solo album by John Frusciante, originally released on March 8, 1994 by American Recordings. The cover art of Niandra LaDes and Usually Just a T-Shirt is a sepia photograph of Frusciante in drag. According to Toni Oswald, Frusciante’s partner at the time of the album’s making, this choice was inspired by Rrose Sélavy, the feminine pseudonym of Marcel Duchamp—the French painter and writer whom Oswald and Frusciante both deeply admired. Frusciante devised the name “Niandra LaDes” as his own feminine alter ego. The phrase “Usually Just a T-Shirt” meanwhile derives .

podcast.body: John Frusciante's debut solo album, described as low-fi, stream of consciousness, made with very basic gear. He stated he did not record it while on heroin, but while he was a heroin addict, and in a later interview, admitted every note was played while on drugs. All songs were recorded in just one take. The album sold 15,000 copies upon its release, and fans were reportedly confused by it. "You cannot separate that album from John's heroin addiction."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Long Strange Trip of John Frusciante Part 1

podcast.body: This album, released in 1994, was described as strange but fantastic, drawing comparisons to Syd Barrett's recordings. The similarities stemmed from unpolished ideas, low recording quality, and peculiar, critical lyrics that blend emotions. It also reflected a period of severe drug abuse and eccentric behavior, similar to Barrett's struggles. "es ese disco típico de las grabaciones de Sidbare de grandes ideas que no terminan de estar pulidas o que no tienen calidad de grabación o que no terminan de estar trabajadas."

srcs.episode: La historia de John Frusciante: Talento, creatividad y guitarras.
